intended_object: The general linear group functor of a K-module V. It sends each commutative K-algebra R to the group Aut_R(V ⊗_K R) of R-linear automorphisms of the scalar extension, and each algebra map R → S to base change of automorphisms (Milne, Algebraic Groups, 2.8). I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and the companion `generalLinearModuleFunctor`.
explanation:
**The object.** `SourceOrderedTensor K V R` is a wrapper type around `V ⊗[K] R`. Its R-module structure is transported along the swap isomorphism `TensorProduct.comm` with `R ⊗[K] V`, so it really is the scalar extension of V, written with V on the left. On objects the functor gives `LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup R (V ⊗ R)`, which is the unit group of `Module.End R (V ⊗ R)`, i.e. Aut_R(V ⊗_K R).

**The maps.** For an algebra map g : R → S, the map on groups is built in three steps:
- conjugate by the swap to get to `R ⊗ V`;
- extend endomorphisms by Mathlib's `Module.End.baseChangeHom`, followed by `cancelBaseChange`, which identifies S ⊗_R (R ⊗_K V) with S ⊗_K V;
- conjugate back.

This is the standard base change of automorphisms: on pure tensors it sends v ⊗ s to s · (g ⊗ id)(f(v ⊗ 1)). The proofs that identities and composites are preserved come from the corresponding lemmas in the same file. The file also builds a natural isomorphism, `sourceOrderedGeneralLinearIso`, from this functor to `generalLinearModuleFunctor`, which is `End ⋙ units`.

**Generality.** K is any commutative ring, V any K-module, and the test algebras are all commutative K-algebras. That is the natural generality for GL_V, so the definition is not too narrow.

**Mathlib.** I searched `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry` for `GeneralLinearGroup` and found nothing, so I don't think this Mathlib version has an automorphism-group functor of a module on `CommAlgCat` (the search was narrow, so this is not exhaustive).
